notes: The clustered template (graphics_owner_13.c, nibble palette decode) does not match this owner's actual behavior -- weak cluster match. Read games/gs1/asm/08022768.s directly instead: a tilemap-rect clip-and-fill over the global Data_03001e8c render-work base pointer (declared elsewhere as `extern u8 *Data_03001e8c;`, same global used by games/gs1/src/ui/window/clear_tile_attributes_in_rect.c). Params (x, y, width, height, alt): clamp x/width and y/height into the 30x20 tile grid (x<0 -> width+=x, x=0; x+width>29 -> width=30-x; same pattern for y/height against 20 rows), then for each row/col in the clamped rect, OR bit 12 with ((alt&1)<<12) into the 16-bit tilemap entry (clearing bit12 first via &0xefff), and after each row OR `2 << (row>>2)` into base[RENDER_DIRTY_OFS] (0xEA3, from games/gs1/include/gs1_edition.h) to mark the touched row-group dirty.

This is a near-twin of main:080ab21c (same family/target array, same clip logic, same dirty-mark tail) with two behavioral differences confirmed from the raw assembly: 08022768 clears+sets bit 12 unconditionally on every tile in the rect (mask 0xffffefff / low16 0xefff), while 080ab21c additionally SKIPS a tile whose low byte equals 0xf (tile>>12 & 0xf == 0xf guard) before touching it, and uses mask 0xffff0fff (clearing the top nibble bits 12-15, a 4-bit field) instead of a single bit. These are genuinely different owners, not the same source respelled twice.

Iterated 4 respellings. Biggest win: replacing a persisted `u16 *cursor` pointer (incremented by 32 halfwords/64 bytes per row, computed once before the loop) with a plain integer byte `offset` recomputed against the base pointer fresh every iteration (`p = (u16*)(base + offset); ...; offset += 64;`) -- this matches the reference's 'adds r4,r6,r5' pattern (rowOffset + base recomputed each loop, rather than a single pointer carried and incremented) and dropped wrong_instructions from 82 to 62.

Residual structural gap: the reference computes the initial byte offset as two INDEPENDENT shifts done in x-then-y order ('lsls r3,r4,#1' (x*2) then 'lsls r2,r1,#6' (y*64) then add), while writing the natural single expression `x*2 + y*64` in the candidate always compiles to a GCD-factored form (y<<5, add x, then <<1 once) regardless of operand order in the source -- tried both `x*2+y*64` and `y*64+x*2`, both factor identically. Tried splitting into two separate statements (`offset = x*2; offset += y*64;`) hoping to prevent the compiler's constant-folding pass from combining across statements; this instead made the match WORSE (wrong_instructions rose to 96) and did not fix the term order, so statement splitting is not the lever. This is very likely a compiler-internal expression-canonicalization difference (which of two mathematically-identical multiply-add sequences the front end emits) rather than something reachable by further manual respelling -- a good candidate for permuter-style search over the offset expression's exact token form.

Remaining smaller diffs are register-number swaps (ip/lr/r8/r9 assignment order) cascading from the above, plus one micro-scheduling difference (whether the outer-loop `height--` lands before or after the `base[RENDER_DIRTY_OFS] |=` store) that looks like pure instruction scheduling, not a source-shape issue.
Not adopted; kept as the closest measured draft. Also relevant to main:080ab21c, which shares this same offset-expression residual (see its own dossier).
